import AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.CodimOneExtension

universe u
open AlgebraicGeometry Order TopologicalSpace CategoryTheory Limits IsLocalRing

namespace Test

theorem isRegularLocalRing_stalk_of_smooth_of_perfectField
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [PerfectField k]
    (X : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [Smooth X.hom]
    (z : X.left) :
    IsRegularLocalRing (X.left.presheaf.stalk z) := by
  obtain ⟨U, hU, V, hV, hzV, e, hSS⟩ :=
    AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.exists_isStandardSmooth X.hom z
  let ε : k ≃+* Γ(Spec (.of k), U) :=
    (gammaSpecField_ringEquiv k U ⟨⟨_, e hzV⟩⟩).symm
  have hSS' : ((X.hom.appLE U V e).hom.comp ε.toRingHom).IsStandardSmooth :=
    RingHom.isStandardSmooth_respectsIso.2 _ ε hSS
  letI : Algebra k Γ(X.left, V) :=
    ((X.hom.appLE U V e).hom.comp ε.toRingHom).toAlgebra
  haveI : Algebra.IsStandardSmooth k Γ(X.left, V) := hSS'.toAlgebra
  letI : Algebra Γ(X.left, V) (X.left.presheaf.stalk z) :=
    TopCat.Presheaf.algebra_section_stalk X.left.presheaf ⟨z, hzV⟩
  haveI hLoc : IsLocalization.AtPrime (X.left.presheaf.stalk z)
      (hV.primeIdealOf ⟨z, hzV⟩).asIdeal :=
    hV.isLocalization_stalk ⟨z, hzV⟩
  have hp : (hV.primeIdealOf ⟨z, hzV⟩).asIdeal.IsPrime := (hV.primeIdealOf ⟨z, hzV⟩).isPrime
  haveI : Nontrivial Γ(X.left, V) := by
    refine ⟨0, 1, fun h => hp.1 ?_⟩
    exact Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem _ (Submodule.zero_mem _) (h ▸ isUnit_one)
  letI : Algebra k (X.left.presheaf.stalk z) :=
    ((algebraMap Γ(X.left, V) (X.left.presheaf.stalk z)).comp
      (algebraMap k Γ(X.left, V))).toAlgebra
  haveI : IsScalarTower k Γ(X.left, V) (X.left.presheaf.stalk z) :=
    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
  exact isRegularLocalRing_of_isLocalization_atPrime_of_isStandardSmooth_of_perfectField
    (k := k) (S := Γ(X.left, V)) _ hp (X.left.presheaf.stalk z)

#print axioms Test.isRegularLocalRing_stalk_of_smooth_of_perfectField

-- Does the new lemma imply the OLD one at the OLD's binders?

    [IsSeparated X.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom]
    [IsIntegral X.left] [IsReduced X.left]

end Test

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.CoheightBridge
7	import Mathlib
8	
9	/-!
10	# Topological Krull dimension of a scheme from its stalks
11	
12	This file supplies the bridge that the dimension leg of the Jacobian A.3 story
13	was recorded as *missing*: a way to compute `topologicalKrullDim X` for a scheme
14	`X` out of local data at the points of `X`.
15	
16	The recorded price (see `Picard/IdentityComponent.lean`, `finrank_eq_genus`, and
17	the same analysis at `Jacobian.lean`) was that mathlib v4.31 has essentially no
18	API for `topologicalKrullDim` — only `IsHomeomorph.topologicalKrullDim_eq`,
19	`IsInducing.topologicalKrullDim_le`, `topologicalKrullDim_subspace_le`,
20	`topologicalKrullDim_zero_of_discreteTopology` and
21	`PrimeSpectrum.topologicalKrullDim_eq_ringKrullDim`, none of which connects the
22	invariant to a tangent-space dimension; the suggested route ran through
23	`Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension` and an affine-local presentation.
24	
25	That analysis measured the wrong side of the problem. `topologicalKrullDim` is
26	*by definition* the order-theoretic `krullDim` of the poset of irreducible closed
27	subsets, and for a scheme that poset is order-isomorphic to the space itself
28	(`irreducibleSetEquivPoints`, since a scheme is sober and `T0`). Under that
29	isomorphism mathlib's `Order.krullDim_eq_iSup_coheight` turns the dimension into
30	a supremum of coheights, and this project already owns
31	`Scheme.ringKrullDim_stalk_eq_coheight` (`Albanese/CoheightBridge.lean`) which
32	identifies each coheight with the Krull dimension of a stalk. So the dimension of
33	a scheme is the supremum of the Krull dimensions of its stalks — and no
34	standard-smooth presentation is required.
35	
36	## Main results
37	
38	* `Scheme.topologicalKrullDim_eq_iSup_ringKrullDim_stalk` — the general identity
39	  `dim X = ⨆ z, dim 𝒪_{X,z}`, for **any** scheme.
40	* `Scheme.topologicalKrullDim_le_of_forall_ringKrullDim_stalk_le` and
41	  `Scheme.ringKrullDim_stalk_le_topologicalKrullDim` — the two halves, combined in
42	  `Scheme.topologicalKrullDim_eq_of_le_of_exists_ge`.
43	* `Scheme.le_topologicalKrullDim_of_finrank_cotangentSpace` — the ≥ half in
44	  cotangent form, from data at a **single** regular point. This is the shape the
45	  tangent-space computation `dim_k T₀ = g` feeds.
46	
47	## A scope warning that shaped the statements
48	
49	Stalks of a scheme do **not** all have the same dimension: at a generic point the
50	stalk is a localisation at a minimal prime, of dimension `0`. So a
51	"constant stalk dimension" hypothesis is nearly vacuous, and the
52	homogeneity of a group scheme does not repair it — translation acts transitively
53	on *closed* points over an algebraically closed field, not on all points. The
54	constant forms are retained (`…_eq_of_forall_ringKrullDim_stalk_eq`,
55	`…_eq_of_forall_finrank_cotangentSpace_eq`) with that warning attached; a real
56	dimension computation pairs a uniform ≤ bound with a ≥ witness at one point.
57	-/
58	
59	universe u
60	
61	open AlgebraicGeometry Order TopologicalSpace CategoryTheory
62	
63	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
64	
65	/-- **The topological Krull dimension of a scheme is the supremum of the Krull
66	dimensions of its stalks.**
67	
68	Proof in three moves, none of them geometric:
69	
70	* `topologicalKrullDim X` is `krullDim (IrreducibleCloseds X)` by definition;
71	* a scheme is sober and `T0`, so `irreducibleSetEquivPoints` is an order
72	  isomorphism `IrreducibleCloseds X ≃o X` (for the specialisation order), and
73	  `Order.krullDim_eq_of_orderIso` transports the dimension to the carrier;
74	* `Order.krullDim_eq_iSup_coheight` writes that as `⨆ z, coheight z`, and the
75	  project's `Scheme.ringKrullDim_stalk_eq_coheight` replaces each coheight by
76	  `ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk z)`.
77	
78	This is the missing bridge referred to at `Picard/IdentityComponent.lean`'s
79	`finrank_eq_genus`: it connects `topologicalKrullDim` to *local* data, which is
80	what any tangent-space computation produces. -/
81	theorem topologicalKrullDim_eq_iSup_ringKrullDim_stalk (X : Scheme.{u}) :
82	    topologicalKrullDim X = ⨆ (z : X), ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk z) := by
83	  have h : topologicalKrullDim X = ⨆ (z : X), (Order.coheight z : WithBot ℕ∞) := by
84	    unfold topologicalKrullDim
85	    rw [Order.krullDim_eq_of_orderIso (irreducibleSetEquivPoints (α := X))]
86	    exact Order.krullDim_eq_iSup_coheight
87	  rw [h]
88	  exact iSup_congr fun z => (ringKrullDim_stalk_eq_coheight X z).symm
89	
90	/-- **A scheme all of whose stalks have Krull dimension `d` has dimension `d`.**
91	
92	The specialisation of `topologicalKrullDim_eq_iSup_ringKrullDim_stalk` to a
93	*constant* stalk dimension. `Nonempty X` is genuinely needed: over an empty
94	scheme the supremum is `⊥`, not `d`.
95	
96	**READ THE SCOPE WARNING BEFORE REACHING FOR THIS.** It is nearly vacuous, and
97	saying so is the point of stating the two bounds below instead. Stalks of a
98	scheme are *not* all of the same dimension: the stalk at a generic point of an
99	irreducible component is a localisation at a minimal prime, so it has dimension
100	`0`, while the stalk at a closed point of a `d`-dimensional variety has dimension
101	`d`. So the hypothesis `∀ z, ringKrullDim (stalk z) = d` forces `d = 0` on any
102	nonempty scheme with a generic point — in particular this lemma says nothing
103	about `Pic⁰` beyond `d = 0`, and the "translation makes all stalks isomorphic"
104	reading of homogeneity is **false**: translation is transitive on *closed* points
105	of a group scheme over an algebraically closed field, not on all points.
106	
107	The useful forms are `topologicalKrullDim_le_of_forall_ringKrullDim_stalk_le`
108	(the ≤ half, quantified over all points) and
109	`ringKrullDim_stalk_le_topologicalKrullDim` (the ≥ half, at one point), combined
110	in `topologicalKrullDim_eq_of_le_of_exists_ge`. -/
111	theorem topologicalKrullDim_eq_of_forall_ringKrullDim_stalk_eq
112	    (X : Scheme.{u}) [Nonempty X] (d : WithBot ℕ∞)
113	    (h : ∀ z : X, ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk z) = d) :
114	    topologicalKrullDim X = d := by
115	  rw [topologicalKrullDim_eq_iSup_ringKrullDim_stalk X]
116	  simp [h]
117	
118	/-- **The ≤ half: a bound at every point bounds the dimension.** Unlike the
119	constant form above this is not vacuous — a bound holding at all points is
120	exactly what "every local ring has dimension at most `d`" says, and it is the
121	half a *smooth* scheme of relative dimension `d` supplies. -/
122	theorem topologicalKrullDim_le_of_forall_ringKrullDim_stalk_le
123	    (X : Scheme.{u}) (d : WithBot ℕ∞)
124	    (h : ∀ z : X, ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk z) ≤ d) :
125	    topologicalKrullDim X ≤ d := by
126	  rw [topologicalKrullDim_eq_iSup_ringKrullDim_stalk X]
127	  exact iSup_le h
128	
129	/-- **The ≥ half: one point's stalk dimension bounds the dimension from below.**
130	The witness may be taken at any single point — for a group scheme, the identity. -/
131	theorem ringKrullDim_stalk_le_topologicalKrullDim
132	    (X : Scheme.{u}) (z : X) :
133	    ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk z) ≤ topologicalKrullDim X := by
134	  rw [topologicalKrullDim_eq_iSup_ringKrullDim_stalk X]
135	  exact le_iSup (fun z : X => ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk z)) z
136	
137	/-- **The honest constant-dimension criterion**: a uniform upper bound at *every*
138	point plus a matching lower bound at *one* point. This is the shape a dimension
139	computation on a variety actually has — the bound comes from smoothness (or a
140	presentation) globally, and the witness from a distinguished closed point, which
141	for `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is the identity. -/
142	theorem topologicalKrullDim_eq_of_le_of_exists_ge
143	    (X : Scheme.{u}) (d : WithBot ℕ∞)
144	    (hle : ∀ z : X, ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk z) ≤ d)
145	    (z₀ : X) (hz₀ : d ≤ ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk z₀)) :
146	    topologicalKrullDim X = d :=
147	  le_antisymm (topologicalKrullDim_le_of_forall_ringKrullDim_stalk_le X d hle)
148	    (hz₀.trans (ringKrullDim_stalk_le_topologicalKrullDim X z₀))
149	
150	/-- **The ≥ half in cotangent form: the embedding dimension at ONE regular point
151	bounds the scheme's dimension from below.**
152	
153	At a regular point, `IsRegularLocalRing.iff_finrank_cotangentSpace` identifies
154	`dim_{κ(z)} m_z/m_z²` with `dim 𝒪_{X,z}`, and that is at most `dim X` by
155	`ringKrullDim_stalk_le_topologicalKrullDim`. `[IsLocallyNoetherian X]` is what
156	makes the stalk Noetherian; for a scheme locally of finite type over a field it
157	is free (`LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian`).

10	/-!
11	# The dimension of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is the genus
12	
13	This file turns the tangent-space identity `dim_{κ(e)} m_e/m_e² = g(C)` at the
14	identity of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` (`Pic0.finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_finrank_hModuleOne`,
15	`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`) into a statement about the **dimension of the
16	scheme** `Pic⁰_{C/k}`, which is what Milne III.1 Rmk 1.4(e) — "the dimension of
17	`J` is the genus of `C`" — asserts and what
18	`Pic0Scheme.finrank_eq_genus` (`Picard/IdentityComponent.lean`) pins.
19	
20	## Two inputs, and which of them was actually missing
21	
22	The recorded blocker at `finrank_eq_genus` was the *dimension-theoretic* step,
23	priced as an absent mathlib API for `topologicalKrullDim`. That step is supplied
24	by `Picard/SchemeKrullDimStalk.lean`, from the definition of the invariant rather
25	than from a presentation. What remains here is the *local algebra*:
26	
27	* **regularity of the stalk** at the point where the tangent space is computed
28	  — `Scheme.isRegularLocalRing_stalk_of_smooth_of_perfectField` below;
29	* the **≥ direction only** comes for free from data at the identity. The ≤
30	  direction genuinely needs information at every point, and is stated as a
31	  hypothesis (see `topologicalKrullDim_eq_genus_of_forall_ringKrullDim_stalk_le`).
32	
33	## The generalisation this file contributes upstream of itself
34	
35	`Albanese/CodimOneExtension.lean` already proves stalk regularity from
36	smoothness, as `isRegularLocalRing_stalk_of_smooth` — but over an
37	**algebraically closed** field, and with `[GeometricallyIrreducible]`,
38	`[IsSeparated]`, `[LocallyOfFiniteType]`, `[IsIntegral]`, `[IsReduced]` binders.
39	None of those is used by the argument: the chart step is mathlib's
40	`Smooth.exists_isStandardSmooth` (Stacks 00T7), which needs only smoothness, and
41	the algebra step is the project's own
42	`isRegularLocalRing_of_isLocalization_atPrime_of_isStandardSmooth_of_perfectField`
43	(`Albanese/SmoothPrimeRegularity.lean`), which needs only `PerfectField`. So the
44	version proved here has `[Field k] [PerfectField k] [Smooth X.hom]` and nothing
45	else.
46	
47	That matters for this lane specifically: `Pic⁰_{C/k}` lives over the *given* base
48	field `k`, not over `k̄`, and no descent step is available for regularity — so the
49	alg-closed version could not have been applied here at all. (`PerfectField` is
50	still an assumption on `k`, and a real one: it holds in characteristic zero and
51	for finite and algebraically closed fields, and fails for e.g. `𝔽_p(t)`.)
52	-/
53

60	/-- **Stalks of a smooth scheme over a perfect field are regular local rings**
61	(Stacks 00TT, Jacobian-criterion direction) — at **every** point, closed or not,
62	with no hypothesis on the scheme beyond smoothness of the structural morphism.
63	
64	Two steps, both already in the tree:
65	
66	* mathlib's `Smooth.exists_isStandardSmooth` (Stacks 00T7) gives an affine chart
67	  `V ∋ z` on which the section ring is standard-smooth over `Γ(Spec k, U)`, and
68	  `gammaSpecField_ringEquiv` identifies that base with `k`;
69	* the stalk is the localisation of `Γ(X, V)` at the prime of `z`
70	  (`IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_stalk`), and the project's Serre-free Stacks-00TT
71	  theorem at an arbitrary prime over a perfect field,
72	  `isRegularLocalRing_of_isLocalization_atPrime_of_isStandardSmooth_of_perfectField`
73	  (`Albanese/SmoothPrimeRegularity.lean`), concludes.
74	
75	**This is a strict generalisation of `isRegularLocalRing_stalk_of_smooth`**
76	(`Albanese/CodimOneExtension.lean`), which asks for `[IsAlgClosed kbar]` plus
77	`[GeometricallyIrreducible]`, `[IsSeparated]`, `[LocallyOfFiniteType]`,
78	`[IsIntegral]` and `[IsReduced]`. What is *measured* here is that the proof below
79	elaborates with all six absent simultaneously and `PerfectField` in place of
80	`IsAlgClosed` — which is the claim that matters, though it does not by itself
81	show each binder is individually unused in the original (that proof is a
82	different proof term). The alg-closedness enters the argument only through
83	`PerfectField`, which `IsAlgClosed` implies.
84	
85	The generalisation is *load-bearing* for the Picard lane, not cosmetic: `Pic⁰_{C/k}`
86	sits over the given field `k`, and regularity of a stalk does not descend along
87	`Spec k̄ → Spec k` by any route in this tree, so the alg-closed form is unusable
88	here. -/
89	theorem isRegularLocalRing_stalk_of_smooth_of_perfectField
90	    {k : Type u} [Field k] [PerfectField k]
91	    (X : Over (Spec (.of k)))
92	    [Smooth X.hom]
93	    (z : X.left) :
94	    IsRegularLocalRing (X.left.presheaf.stalk z) := by
95	  obtain ⟨U, hU, V, hV, hzV, e, hSS⟩ :=
96	    AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.exists_isStandardSmooth X.hom z
97	  -- Base identification `Γ(Spec k, U) ≃+* k`: `U` contains the image of `z`, so it
98	  -- is nonempty.
99	  let ε : k ≃+* Γ(Spec (.of k), U) :=
100	    (gammaSpecField_ringEquiv k U ⟨⟨_, e hzV⟩⟩).symm
101	  have hSS' : ((X.hom.appLE U V e).hom.comp ε.toRingHom).IsStandardSmooth :=
102	    RingHom.isStandardSmooth_respectsIso.2 _ ε hSS
103	  letI : Algebra k Γ(X.left, V) :=
104	    ((X.hom.appLE U V e).hom.comp ε.toRingHom).toAlgebra
105	  haveI : Algebra.IsStandardSmooth k Γ(X.left, V) := hSS'.toAlgebra
106	  letI : Algebra Γ(X.left, V) (X.left.presheaf.stalk z) :=
107	    TopCat.Presheaf.algebra_section_stalk X.left.presheaf ⟨z, hzV⟩
108	  haveI hLoc : IsLocalization.AtPrime (X.left.presheaf.stalk z)
109	      (hV.primeIdealOf ⟨z, hzV⟩).asIdeal :=
110	    hV.isLocalization_stalk ⟨z, hzV⟩
111	  have hp : (hV.primeIdealOf ⟨z, hzV⟩).asIdeal.IsPrime := (hV.primeIdealOf ⟨z, hzV⟩).isPrime
112	  haveI : Nontrivial Γ(X.left, V) := by
113	    refine ⟨0, 1, fun h => hp.1 ?_⟩
114	    exact Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem _ (Submodule.zero_mem _) (h ▸ isUnit_one)
115	  letI : Algebra k (X.left.presheaf.stalk z) :=
116	    ((algebraMap Γ(X.left, V) (X.left.presheaf.stalk z)).comp
117	      (algebraMap k Γ(X.left, V))).toAlgebra
118	  haveI : IsScalarTower k Γ(X.left, V) (X.left.presheaf.stalk z) :=
119	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
120	  exact isRegularLocalRing_of_isLocalization_atPrime_of_isStandardSmooth_of_perfectField
121	    (k := k) (S := Γ(X.left, V)) _ hp (X.left.presheaf.stalk z)

123	namespace Pic0
124	
125	/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is locally Noetherian** — free from finite type over a field,
126	via `Pic0.locallyOfFiniteType` and mathlib's
127	`LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian`. Needed to make the stalks Noetherian,
128	which is what `IsRegularLocalRing.iff_finrank_cotangentSpace` consumes. -/
129	theorem isLocallyNoetherian {k : Type u} [Field k]
130	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
131	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
132	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C]
133	    [PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C] :
134	    IsLocallyNoetherian (Pic0Scheme C).left := by
135	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (Pic0Scheme C).hom := Pic0.locallyOfFiniteType C
136	  exact LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian (Pic0Scheme C).hom
137	
138	/-- **The genus is a LOWER bound for the dimension of `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** — proved,
139	modulo regularity of the single stalk at the identity.
140	
141	This is the half of Milne III.1 Rmk 1.4(e) that the tangent-space computation
142	gives away for free, and it needs data at **one** point:
143	
144	* `Pic0.finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_finrank_hModuleOne` computes
145	  `dim_{κ(e)} m_e/m_e² = dim_k H¹(C, 𝒪_C) = g(C)` at the identity;
146	* at a regular point `IsRegularLocalRing.iff_finrank_cotangentSpace` turns that
147	  into `dim 𝒪_{Pic⁰, e} = g(C)`;
148	* and a stalk's dimension is at most the dimension of the scheme
149	  (`ringKrullDim_stalk_le_topologicalKrullDim`, from
150	  `Picard/SchemeKrullDimStalk.lean`).
151	
152	Note what is *not* needed: no quantifier over the points of `Pic⁰`, no smoothness
153	of `Pic⁰` (only regularity at `e`), and no affine-local presentation — the
154	recorded route through `Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension` is not
155	taken. -/
156	theorem genus_le_topologicalKrullDim_of_isRegular {k : Type u} [Field k]
157	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
158	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
159	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C]
160	    [PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C]
161	    (hreg : IsRegularLocalRing ((Pic0Scheme C).left.presheaf.stalk
162	      ((identitySection C).base default))) :
163	    ((AlgebraicGeometry.genus C : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞)
164	      ≤ topologicalKrullDim (Pic0Scheme C).left := by
165	  haveI := isLocallyNoetherian C
166	  exact le_topologicalKrullDim_of_finrank_cotangentSpace _ _ _ hreg
167	    (finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_finrank_hModuleOne C)
168	
169	/-- **The genus lower bound, with regularity discharged from smoothness over a
170	perfect field.**
171	
172	`Pic⁰_{C/k}` smooth over `k` (which is what `Pic0.smooth` asserts, and what
173	`Pic0.smooth_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange` reduces to reducedness over
174	`k̄`) gives regularity of *every* stalk by
175	`Scheme.isRegularLocalRing_stalk_of_smooth_of_perfectField`, in particular at the
176	identity. So over a perfect base field the lower bound needs no regularity
177	hypothesis at all — only smoothness, which is front (b) of this chapter. -/
178	theorem genus_le_topologicalKrullDim_of_smooth {k : Type u} [Field k] [PerfectField k]
179	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
180	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
181	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C]
182	    [PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C]
183	    (hsm : Smooth (Pic0Scheme C).hom) :
184	    ((AlgebraicGeometry.genus C : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞)
185	      ≤ topologicalKrullDim (Pic0Scheme C).left := by
186	  haveI := hsm
187	  exact genus_le_topologicalKrullDim_of_isRegular C
188	    (Scheme.isRegularLocalRing_stalk_of_smooth_of_perfectField (Pic0Scheme C) _)
189	
190	/-- **`dim Pic⁰_{C/k} = g(C)`** — Milne III.1 Rmk 1.4(e), from smoothness over a
191	perfect field plus a uniform upper bound on the local dimensions.
192	
193	This is the honest factoring of `Pic0Scheme.finrank_eq_genus`
194	(`Picard/IdentityComponent.lean`), and it makes visible that the two directions
195	have genuinely different costs:
196	
197	* **≥** is discharged here, from the tangent-space identity at the identity alone
198	  (`genus_le_topologicalKrullDim_of_smooth`);
199	* **≤** is the hypothesis `hle`, and it cannot be obtained from data at one
200	  point: it says every local ring of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` has dimension at most `g`. On a
201	  smooth *equidimensional* scheme this is the statement that the relative
202	  dimension is `g`, i.e. exactly the content of
203	  `SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (Pic0Scheme C).hom`, which
204	  `Picard/IdentityComponent.lean` already flags as the cheaper target for
205	  consumers wanting a dimension index.
206	
207	So the remaining open content of the dimension statement is one *uniform* bound,
208	with the tangent-space side fully consumed. -/
209	theorem topologicalKrullDim_eq_genus_of_forall_ringKrullDim_stalk_le
210	    {k : Type u} [Field k] [PerfectField k]
211	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
212	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
213	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C]
214	    [PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C]
215	    (hsm : Smooth (Pic0Scheme C).hom)
216	    (hle : ∀ z : (Pic0Scheme C).left,
217	      ringKrullDim ((Pic0Scheme C).left.presheaf.stalk z)
218	        ≤ ((AlgebraicGeometry.genus C : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
219	    topologicalKrullDim (Pic0Scheme C).left
220	      = ((AlgebraicGeometry.genus C : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) :=
221	  le_antisymm
222	    (Scheme.topologicalKrullDim_le_of_forall_ringKrullDim_stalk_le _ _ hle)
223	    (genus_le_topologicalKrullDim_of_smooth C hsm)
224	
225	end Pic0

227	end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
